claims.statement: getUserGitHubToken is the canonical two-tier GitHub token reader: it resolves the current session, then SELECTs accounts.accessToken WHERE userId matches and provider='github' first, falling back to SELECTing users.accessToken WHERE id matches and provider='github' on miss, decrypting whichever row wins, and returning null on either miss or a thrown decrypt error.

getOctokit in lib/github/client.ts is the single Octokit factory: it asks getUserGitHubToken for the token, returns new Octokit({ auth: token || undefined }) so callers can check octokit.auth as a boolean, and warns to the server console when no token is available rather than throwing.

lib/github/client.ts exports five high-level helpers that wrap specific Octokit endpoints and translate known status codes into domain-level error messages: getGitHubUser (users.getAuthenticated, returns null on any error), createPullRequest (pulls.create; 422 already-exists, 403 permission, 404 missing), mergePullRequest (pulls.merge with default mergeMethod='squash'; 405 not-mergeable, 409 conflict, 403/404), getPullRequestStatus (pulls.get; maps merged_at/state to 'merged'/'closed'/'open'), and parseGitHubUrl (regex-only, returns { owner, repo } or null, accepts HTTPS and SSH forms).

The repository browser at /repos/[owner]/[repo] is a Next.js shell with three sibling tab routes (commits, issues, pull-requests), each implemented as a one-line server-component page that renders a single client component (RepoCommits, RepoIssues, RepoPullRequests). The shared layout in components/repo-layout.tsx drives navigation from a tabs array of { name, href } pairs whose active state is computed by comparing usePathname() to each tab's href, and the default page.tsx redirects to /commits.

Each repo-browser tab fetches from a dedicated GET API route that calls a single Octokit method bounded to 30 results: /api/repos/[owner]/[repo]/commits uses repos.listCommits, /issues uses issues.listForRepo with state='open' (filtering out issues that have a pull_request field), and /pull-requests uses pulls.list with state='open' sorted by updated desc.

The PR tab calls GET /api/repos/[owner]/[repo]/pull-requests/[pr_number]/check-task for each open PR to mark rows that already have a task (and hide the Create Task menu item accordingly), and exposes a Close PR dropdown action that PATCHes /api/repos/[owner]/[repo]/pull-requests/[pr_number]/close. The close route calls octokit.rest.pulls.update({ state: 'closed' }); the check-task route SELECTs tasks where userId, prNumber, and repoUrl all match.

Five task-scoped endpoints under app/api/tasks/[taskId]/ implement the PR lifecycle: POST /pr (createPullRequest, sets prUrl/prNumber/prStatus='open', short-circuits with alreadyExists when task.prUrl is set), POST /merge-pr (mergePullRequest, sets prStatus='merged' and completedAt, tears down the sandbox), POST /close-pr (pulls.update state='closed'), POST /reopen-pr (pulls.update state='open'), and POST /sync-pr (getPullRequestStatus, sets prStatus/prMergeCommitSha and completedAt when the new state is merged).

The merge-pr endpoint stops the live sandbox as part of a successful merge: it calls Sandbox.get with the task's sandboxId, invokes sandbox.stop(), unregisters it via unregisterSandbox(taskId), then clears sandboxId and sandboxUrl on the task row. The teardown is wrapped in try/catch so a sandbox failure is logged but does not roll back the merge DB write.

app/api/github/repos/create/route.ts is the only route under app/api/github/ that uses Octokit: it validates the name with /^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/, then dispatches on owner — calling octokit.repos.createForAuthenticatedUser when owner equals users.getAuthenticated().login, otherwise octokit.repos.createInOrg (mapping a 404 to 403 'Organization not found or you do not have permission to create repositories'). When a template is supplied, populateRepoFromTemplate recursively walks the source via octokit.repos.getContent and seeds files via octokit.repos.createOrUpdateFileContents, continuing past per-file failures.

Five of the six routes under app/api/github/ (user, orgs, repos, user-repos, verify-repo) call raw fetch against https://api.github.com/* with a Bearer header rather than using Octokit. The repos route paginates per_page=100, deduplicates by full_name, and dispatches between /user/repos, /orgs/{owner}/repos, and /users/{owner}/repos based on whether the owner is the authenticated user. The verify-repo route returns 200 { accessible: false } for a GitHub 404 so the UI can branch on the boolean.

For the copilot agent, lib/sandbox/agents/index.ts dynamically imports getUserGitHubToken, and when a token is returned it is written into process.env.GH_TOKEN and process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN for the lifetime of that agent run, so the copilot CLI inside the sandbox can authenticate against the GitHub API on the user's behalf.

The Octokit REST methods actually invoked across the GitHub integration are: users.getAuthenticated (getGitHubUser, repos/create owner check), repos.createForAuthenticatedUser and repos.createInOrg (repos/create), repos.getContent (repos/create template seeder, port-detection package.json), repos.createOrUpdateFileContents (repos/create template seeder), repos.listCommits (commits tab), issues.listForRepo (issues tab), pulls.list (pull-requests tab), pulls.get (getPullRequestStatus, used by sync-pr), pulls.create (createPullRequest, used by pr), pulls.update (close, reopen, repo-browser close), pulls.merge (mergePullRequest, used by merge-pr), and checks.listForRef (check-runs).
